subject: AI & Agents
title: Narrow AI vs General AI
description: A 60-second lesson on Narrow AI vs General AI.

hook.text: Siri can set a timer but can't explain why a joke is funny.

buildup.text: Today's AI is 'narrow' — brilliant at one task, useless at everything else.

discovery.text: General AI would handle any intellectual task a human can. It doesn't exist yet.

twist.text: Chess engines crushed grandmasters in 1997 but couldn't play tic-tac-toe without retraining.

climax.text: Every AI product you use today is narrow — including the ones that feel magical.

punchline.text: Today's AI is a specialist, not a generalist.

quiz.question: What is 'narrow AI'?
options: AI that excels at one specific task
AI that only works on small datasets

details.summary: Narrow AI excels at one specific task like image recognition or language translation. General AI would handle any intellectual task like a human. All current AI is narrow; general AI remains theoretical.
details.whyItMatters: Confusing narrow AI with general AI fuels both hype and fear. Knowing that every AI system today is a specialist, not a generalist, anchors expectations in reality.
takeaways: All current AI systems are narrow, specialized for specific tasks
General AI would match human-level reasoning across all domains
No general AI exists and there is no clear path to creating one

faq.question: Is ChatGPT an example of general AI?
faq.answer: No. Despite its versatility, ChatGPT is narrow AI optimized for text generation. It cannot perceive the physical world, learn from experience, or reason flexibly about novel situations the way a human can.

faq.question: When will we have general AI?
faq.answer: There is no consensus. Some researchers predict decades; others believe it may never be achieved with current approaches. The gap between narrow AI and genuine general intelligence remains enormous.
